deep_research_assignment.title: Modernizing Marlowe: A Decision-Grade Language, Formal-Semantics, Runtime, Tooling, Governance, and Adoption Strategy for Marlowe V2 and Beyond
deep_research_assignment.candidate_enduring_thesis:
Evaluate, rather than blindly assume, that a modern Marlowe should retain these principles:
1. Marlowe is a financial-agreement DSL, not a general-purpose smart-contract language. 2. Every contract is finite or otherwise has a statically provable resource and lifetime bound. 3. All branches, waits, and non-cooperation contingencies are explicit. 4. Contract behavior is inspectable by domain experts and analyzable by machines. 5. Value conservation and payout behavior are part of the semantic model. 6. The maximum lifetime and execution-resource envelope can be determined before deployment. 7. A universal or small family of audited validators can execute many contracts without each contract requiring a new audit. 8. High-level source convenience must not enlarge the trusted on-chain kernel without strong justification. 9. Off-chain services may improve usability, but correctness should not silently depend on trusting a particular Runtime operator. 10. The distinction among semantic safety, ledger executability, participant liveness, data availability, and application security must remain explicit.

deep_research_assignment.workstream_1_current_system_reconstructi:
Reconstruct Marlowe V1 precisely.
Produce:
1. The complete abstract syntax and data model for contracts, actions, inputs, values, observations, parties, payees, tokens, accounts, choices, timeouts, state, warnings, payments, and transaction results. 2. The operational flow through interval fixing, reduction to quiescence, input application, transaction computation, and continuation selection. 3. The meaning and consequences of each warning and error. 4. The relationship among source representations, JSON encoding, object bundles, linked objects, contract hashes, and Merkleized continuations. 5. The lifecycle of a contract from authoring through simulation, analysis, deployment, transaction construction, validation, indexing, payout, and closure. 6. The exact authorization model for addresses, roles, role tokens, open roles, and payouts. 7. The assumptions that make the abstract semantics blockchain-agnostic and the points at which the Cardano realization is not blockchain-agnostic. 8. The trusted computing base for each supported user workflow. 9. A system-context diagram, component diagram, transaction sequence diagram, and data/provenance diagram.
deep_research_assignment.workstream_7_modernization_architectures:
Develop and compare at least these four coherent alternatives.
Maintain the existing language semantics, concentrating on documentation, compatibility, Runtime simplification, cost improvements, security, tooling, and governance.
Treat this as a serious baseline rather than a straw man.
Evolve the existing core directly with a tightly limited set of V2 constructs, broadly following the official V2.0 proposal.
Optimize for continuity, reduced implementation burden, and preservation of existing mental and formal models.
Define a smaller or comparably small Marlowe Core 2 as the authoritative executable kernel.
Add a modern typed surface language that may provide:
- modules and imports; - named definitions; - parameterized templates; - typed functions or macros that elaborate away; - records and domain data used at compile time; - generics over parties, tokens, and schedules; - bounded loops, folds, and comprehensions; - relative-time expressions; - typed amounts and units; - pattern-like construction; - reusable packages; - and better diagnostics.
Require elaboration to produce a finite core contract with an explicit resource, transaction, and lifetime bound before deployment.
Investigate whether the surface compiler can be verified, proof-producing, translation-validated, or sufficiently checked through differential and property testing.
Treat Marlowe as a typed financial state-machine and transaction-intent language that can safely compose with external validators, minting policies, credentials, oracles, and application logic.
Define explicit capability and trust boundaries rather than embedding arbitrary Plutus behavior inside the Marlowe semantic kernel.
Investigate typed foreign calls, transaction constraints, effect declarations, capability manifests, script-hash allowlists, and compositional audit evidence.
Explore whether the blockchain-agnostic semantics should have multiple execution backends, including Cardano L1, Hydra or another state-channel environment, or additional ledgers.
Do not recommend portability merely because it is technically possible. Identify the common semantic substrate, unavoidable backend differences, security models, liquidity assumptions, and realistic demand.
Score all options using the decision framework below. Hybrid proposals are permitted, but their boundaries must be exact.
deep_research_assignment.required_experiments:
At minimum, perform or specify reproducibly:
1. V1-versus-V2 implementation of the representative contract suite. 2. A recurring-payment contract with 10, 100, and 1,000 periods, comparing unrolling and bounded iteration. 3. A high-participant close and payout benchmark. 4. A WhenAll or action-set concurrency test covering ordering, partial submission, atomicity, and timeout. 5. A typed-value experiment demonstrating unit and token errors caught before deployment. 6. A state-compression benchmark measuring datum, transaction, execution, storage, and proof impacts. 7. A Merkleized-continuation availability failure exercise. 8. An invalid-initial-state exercise. 9. A role-token monetary-policy attack and recovery analysis. 10. An oracle staleness, replay, and equivocation exercise. 11. A Runtime-compromise exercise in which the client verifies or rejects a maliciously constructed transaction. 12. Differential semantics tests across every maintained implementation. 13. A V1-to-V2 migration dry run on representative deployed contracts. 14. A small user study comparing V1, the candidate V2 surface language, TypeScript construction, and Blockly. 15. A proof-effort prototype for the two or three highest-risk proposed language constructs.

required_deliverables.deliverable_2_evidence_inventory: A source, repository, version, deployment, and status inventory with contradictions and documentation drift highlighted.
required_deliverables.deliverable_3_current_architecture: A complete V1 language and platform architecture, lifecycle, data-flow, trust-boundary, and repository-dependency model.
required_deliverables.deliverable_4_language_and_semantics_dos: A precise account of current syntax, semantics, serialization, authorization, time, value, state, analysis, warnings, and errors.
required_deliverables.deliverable_5_formal_assurance_matrix: The theorem, assumption, implementation-correspondence, and proof-gap matrix.
required_deliverables.deliverable_6_empirical_benchmark: Reproducible contract, cost, size, transaction, usability, and failure benchmarks using current protocol parameters.
required_deliverables.deliverable_7_v2_proposal_audit: A proposal-by-proposal disposition table for all existing Marlowe V2 ideas.
required_deliverables.deliverable_8_comparative_analysis: A comparison that extracts transferable language, verification, transaction-composition, runtime, and tooling patterns from other systems.
required_deliverables.deliverable_9_architecture_options: Full descriptions and weighted scorecards for the stabilization, conservative V2, verified-core-plus-surface-language, composable-protocol, and portable/L2 alternatives.
required_deliverables.deliverable_11_platform_architecture: Specify validators, Runtime, API, SDK, authoring tools, continuation storage, explorer, oracle integration, and deployment architecture.
required_deliverables.deliverable_12_security_plan: End-to-end threat model, trusted-computing-base analysis, audit boundaries, secure-development process, and incident-response requirements.
required_deliverables.deliverable_13_verification_and_test_pla: Normative-specification decision, proof roadmap, conformance suite, differential-test plan, fuzzing strategy, cost gates, and release gates.
required_deliverables.deliverable_14_migration_plan: V1/V2 coexistence, translator, equivalence checking, API migration, validator registry, explorer support, deprecation, rollback, and long-term-support policy.
required_deliverables.deliverable_15_repository_and_governance: Target repository structure, code ownership, release train, semantic versioning policy, MIP improvements, specification authority, audit process, and maintenance model.

deep_research_assignment.final_required_answer:
End with a direct recommendation in this form:
1. Preserve: the exact Marlowe principles and V1 constructs that should remain.
2. Change in V2.0: the smallest coherent, formally defensible, deployable modernization.
3. Develop for V2.1: capabilities requiring further semantics, proofs, experiments, or infrastructure.
4. Move outside the core: features better implemented in the surface language, libraries, Runtime, oracle protocol, transaction-composition layer, or applications.
5. Reject: proposals whose safety, complexity, migration, cost, or demand tradeoff is unfavorable.
6. Prove and test: the exact formal, security, conformance, and empirical work required before release.
7. Migrate: the exact V1/V2 coexistence and compatibility strategy.
8. Build: the 90-day, 12-month, and 24-month implementation sequence.
9. Govern: the specification, repository, release, audit, and MIP process.
10. Validate demand: the pilots and adoption evidence required to justify continued investment.
